title: Ozero Mail
description: Ozero Mail: a private mail app for all your accounts on Android and iOS. No AI, no subscription, nothing in between.
h1: One inbox. No AI. Nothing in between.
sub: A private mail app for all your accounts, on Android and iOS. This page is an inbox too: read it, then clear it.
tip: Scroll to read. Swipe a letter left or tap Done to clear it.
name: Khizri
s1: I tried every mail app. None fit.
s2: I don’t read your mail. Neither does a robot.
s3: Six things I’m building it to do
s7: Why not Apple Mail, Spark or Gmail?
m1a: The private ones felt like settings panels. The friendly ones fed my mail to AI. So I’m building the one I want to use every day.
m1b: There’s no corporation, team or investor behind it. If you ever pay for it, the money goes to me.
shotLabel: The app’s unified inbox: letters from four accounts, each with its own color stripe
wipText: All of this is being built right now. The app isn’t out yet, and details may change.
rc4: Ozero Deep, planned: your own rules, templates, send later, saved searches, settings sync
proNote: Ozero Deep is a plan for now, after the free app ships. Once it’s out, try any of it for 14 days, no card needed.
tipText: Free is enough? Great. If you still want to thank me, there’s a tip jar.
cSubj: Tell me when Ozero Mail is out
cText: Hi! Write me once, on launch day. Nothing else.
cFine: Opens your mail app. Your address stays in my inbox and nowhere else.
statsText: This site counts visits without cookies.
foot1: No AI. No ads. No tracking.

client.fin: Not reading everything is fine. Swipe the rest away, or skip to the note below.
client.finDone: All clear. Calm water. One last note, if you like:

privacy: No AI summaries, no AI replies. Not now, not in Ozero Deep.
Sorting happens on your phone, by rules you can read.
Your mail goes from your provider straight to your phone. My servers never see it.

features.p: Every account in one list, each with its own color.
Done archives a letter. Snooze brings it back later.
Every control within reach of your thumb.
Opens instantly, syncs quietly in the background.
Services and newsletters wait in their own tabs.
Built separately for Android and for iOS.

comparison.p: Good if all your devices are Apple. Ozero Mail works on Android too.
Built around their own service, with AI assistants built in.
A great inbox, but extras come by subscription, and AI is built in.
Private, but heavy on settings. Ozero Mail is made for one hand.

promises.p: Free stays free. Nothing moves behind a paywall.
Your password goes to your provider, never to me.
A public roadmap and a changelog for every update.

questions.a: No. I never get a copy. Instant alerts for Gmail and Outlook pass through a tiny relay. It keeps only a hashed account ID and your phone’s push token, and only hears “something new arrived”.
That’s the plan: Gmail, Outlook, iCloud, Fastmail and any IMAP mail, as many accounts as you like. Exchange without Microsoft 365 and Proton aren’t in the first version.

questions.q: What if you stop working on it?
questions.a: The app doesn’t need my servers to work with your mail, so it keeps working. Your mail stays with your provider, and an Ozero Deep you bought stays yours.
It’s Russian for “lake”, and it ends in “zero”. Calm water, empty inbox.
Phones first. The core is built so it can come to iPad and Mac later, but there’s no date yet.
Yes. Mail you’ve synced opens without a connection, and what you do waits in a queue until you’re back online. Attachments download when you tap them.
Plain checks of the email’s headers, like “has an unsubscribe link, so it’s a newsletter”. They run on your phone and send nothing anywhere.

log.text: Swipe to Done with Undo, People, Services and Newsletters tabs, conversations, search, sending with Undo, new mail notifications, and more than one account.
First real mail on Android and iOS: sign in to an IMAP account, see the inbox, read a letter. HTML mail opens in a locked view with no scripts.
A clickable prototype, and the plan: one shared core for mail, sync and storage, with a native app for each phone.
